Since \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\) are orthogonal, the projections of a vector onto \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\) are perpendicular components that add to the original vector.

So,
\[
\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}
=
\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}
+
\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

Given
\[
\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix},
\]
we get
\[
\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}
-
\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix} -6 \\ 9 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}-6\\9\end{pmatrix}\).
